answer: Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 38 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. The anchor debit happens at intake, hollow totals the burned amount, and basalt anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm hence pays the burn once for every alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. Each impostor pays 19 dollars up front. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
